title: Solar System field guide
description: An image-led science infographic with scale, comparison, timeline, glossary, and sources.
content: Solar System field guide with a planet comparison, orbital-period chart, formation timeline, glossary, and sources.

metadata.subtitle: Eight planets, one star, and 4.6 billion years of history.

blocks.title: A field guide to our planetary neighborhood
blocks.subtitle: Distances and positions below are illustrative; planet facts use NASA reference data.

blocks.title: The planetary system
blocks.alt: Illustrated Solar System with the Sun and the eight named planets on nested orbits.
blocks.caption: The Sun contains about 99.8% of the Solar System's mass. Illustration is not to scale.

blocks.title: Eight worlds, radically different years
blocks.subtitle: A year is one trip around the Sun. Size is diameter, rounded to the nearest kilometer.

blocks.title: How long a year lasts
blocks.description: Orbital periods in Earth years; a logarithmic-looking contrast without pretending that it is a live metric.

blocks.title: Extremes
blocks.content: **Largest:** Jupiter. **Hottest surface:** Venus, whose dense atmosphere traps heat. **Fastest year:** Mercury. **Longest year:** Neptune.

blocks.title: What counts as a planet?
blocks.content: A planet orbits the Sun, is nearly round, and has cleared most neighboring objects from its orbital path.

items.title: A cloud collapses
items.content: Gravity pulls gas and dust into a spinning disk around the young Sun.

items.title: Planets assemble
items.content: Small bodies collide and grow; rocky worlds form close to the Sun.

items.title: A mature system
items.content: Eight planets remain in stable, distinct orbits.

blocks.content:
**Orbit** — the path of one body around another.

**Astronomical unit (AU)** — the average Earth–Sun distance, about 150 million km.

**Gas giant** — a large planet made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

**Ice giant** — a planet rich in water-, ammonia-, and methane-derived ices.

sources.title: Resolution B5: Definition of a Planet
